transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Oh, hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I, um... I hope I'm not taking up an appointment someone else might need more. 

It's just... well, I came in because I can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. It's actually a little embarrassing to admit, because I've always tried to be a good homemaker, but... right now, my kitchen table is just completely covered. It's got all my husband’s appointment papers, and some church flyers, notes from the senior center, and... well, just a lot of half-finished lists. 

I feel so foolish even saying it out loud, but I just sit there looking at it all, not knowing which thing I'm supposed to do first. And then, before I know it, the whole day is just gone. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.

Can you tell me more about those moments when you're sitting at the table not knowing where to start? Does that happen often, and does it leave you feeling stuck even when you want to get things done?

Yes, exactly... like I was just saying, it's that kitchen table. I really do *want* to get it all sorted out, I promise I do. But to answer your question... yes, it seems to be happening almost every day now. 

I'll pull up a chair, thinking, "Okay, I'm going to file my husband's medical papers today," but then I see the church flyers underneath, and those notes from the senior center... and I just freeze. I mean, I'm sure every woman my age gets a little behind on her paperwork sometimes. It's not a terrible crime, right? 

But... I really do just sit there, completely stuck. I have all the best intentions to finish those lists I started, I really do. I just... can't seem to figure out the right order to do them in anymore, and then before I've even started, the afternoon is just gone. 

Does that sound silly? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of a little clutter, Doctor. Am I answering your question alright?
Do you ever feel that certain thoughts keep coming into your mind, even if you don’t want them to, or do you feel the need to do things in a very specific way to make yourself feel better?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think I have anything like that. I mean, I'm not... I don't have any strange thoughts or anything, I promise. 

I just... well, I don't have to do things in a certain way to feel better. If anything, my problem is that I don't have *any* way of doing things right now! I'm just a bit disorganized, that's all. It's nothing... nothing serious like that. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have those kinds of thoughts? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I'm just a little scatterbrained, really. Is that what you were asking, Doctor?
Doctor: Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, even when there isn’t a clear reason for it?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or... or down like that. I mean, I still love seeing my grandchildren and going to my church group when I can. 

I'm generally a very happy person, I really am. I don't want you to think I'm sitting around crying or anything, because I'm definitely not. It's just... well, sometimes it's hard to get the energy to *do* the things I enjoy when I know that kitchen table is waiting for me, you know? But I still love them. 

I really try to keep a positive attitude, Doctor. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I'm not depressed or anything, just... just a little overwhelmed, maybe. Is that okay to say?
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

Oh, no, not really. I mean, I'm 70 years old, so I suppose I don't have the boundless energy of a teenager anymore, but I'm not unusually tired. 

I sleep just fine, and I make sure to get up and get dressed every morning. I don't want you to think I'm just lying in bed all day, because I certainly am not. I try to keep active, you know, going to the grocery store or tending to my little indoor plants. 

It's just that mental tiredness, I suppose, when I look at all the things I'm supposed to be organizing. But physically? Oh, I'm doing just fine for my age, I promise. I hope that's alright? I just want to make sure I'm not making things sound worse than they are, Doctor.
Doctor: Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still, especially when you're trying to get things done?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think I have anything like that. I'm not... I don't pace around or fidget, I promise. I can sit perfectly still when I need to. I'm really a very calm person, usually. 

And I don't think I'm moving any slower than normal, either. I mean, I take my time walking so I don't trip, just to be safe, but I'm not sluggish or anything like that. I usually just sit quietly at my table and... well, look at my papers, mostly. But my body feels just fine, no restlessness at all. 

I hope it's not unhelpful that I keep saying no to these things? I know you're asking them for a good reason, and I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you and giving you what you need. Am I doing alright with these questions, Doctor?
Have you been having trouble making decisions, even about small things, that’s been bothering you lately?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I have trouble making decisions. I mean, I know what I like and what I want to do. I don't sit around agonizing over what to have for breakfast or what to wear, I promise. 

I think I'm pretty decisive, really. It's just... well, when it comes to sorting through all those papers on my table, it's not so much that I can't decide what to do with them, it's just that I don't always know where to start. But that's not the same thing as being indecisive, is it? 

I can always make up my mind when it's important. I hope that makes sense? I really don't want you to think I'm just helpless or can't manage my own life, because I certainly can. I'm doing okay answering these, aren't I, Doctor?
Have you been feeling like you're not good enough or blaming yourself for things more than usual lately?

Oh, heavens, no. I don't think poorly of myself at all, I promise. I mean... I know I get a little scattered with my organizing, like I mentioned, but I don't sit around feeling like I'm not good enough. 

I try to keep a very positive attitude about things. I really don't want to come across as a complainer or someone who just feels sorry for herself, because I'm definitely not. I know I have my little quirks, but I don't blame myself for them in some terrible way. I know I'm a good person who's just trying her best. 

Is that... does that help, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information and not making things too complicated for you.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about not being able to get organized, even when you know it's not a serious problem?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I'm anxious. I mean, I don't sit around worrying myself sick over it, I promise. It's just a little bit of clutter, really, nothing to lose sleep over. 

I know it's not a big deal, and I certainly don't let it get me all worked up. I'm a very peaceful person, usually. I just... well, sometimes I look at the table and think, "Oh, I really should tidy that up," but it doesn't make me feel frightened or panicked or anything like that. I don't want you to think I'm some sort of nervous wreck, because I'm really quite calm. 

I just take it one day at a time. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I'm trying so hard to be clear for you, Doctor. Am I doing okay?
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in most things, even if you couldn't explain why?

Oh, my goodness, no. I've never felt hopeless like that, really. I mean, everyone has a slightly gloomy afternoon here or there, don't they? But not for two weeks, and certainly not where I lose interest in things. 

I've always been someone who tries to find the bright side. I still enjoy my little routines and going for walks. I wouldn't want you to think I'm depressed or just giving up on things, because I'm absolutely not. I try to be very cheerful, even when things get a bit disorganized. 

I don't have anything like that to report, I promise. I hope that's alright? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong impression about my mood, Doctor. I'm doing my best to be helpful, really I am.
Has this difficulty with organizing things on your kitchen table caused problems in other areas of your life, like managing your finances, keeping up with appointments, or maintaining relationships?

Oh, well... I wouldn't call them big problems, exactly. Just, oh, little adjustments here and there, really. I mean... I did recently decide to step down from leading this lovely big event we put on at the senior center. It was just... well, there were so many moving parts, and I told myself it was time to let someone else have a turn, even though I was honestly a bit sad to give it up. 

And, um... as for the bills and appointments... my daughter has been so very sweet. She’s actually started coming over to double-check my mail and my calendar. I try to look at it as her just wanting to be helpful, but... well, if I'm being perfectly honest, she did say she's doing it because she doesn't quite trust that I can keep everything straight on my own anymore. 

It’s a little embarrassing to admit that out loud, to be honest. I absolutely hate the idea of her feeling like she has to manage me, because I really do try so hard to stay on top of things. I hope I don't sound completely incapable to you, Doctor. I'm still trying my very best. Is this the sort of information you needed to know? I hope I'm being helpful.
Have you ever had a time when you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, and lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even for a short while?

Oh, goodness, I think... didn't we just touch on something similar a moment ago? I am so sorry if I wasn't clear before, I'd hate for you to think I was being evasive or confusing. 

But truly, even for a short while, I haven't felt down like that. I mean, of course, everyone has a passing moment of frustration here and there, especially when things get a bit jumbled, but feeling low most of the day? No, I really don't experience that. I still very much enjoy my days and my little activities, I promise. I try to be a very positive person, I really do. 

I hope it's alright that my answer is still no? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know. Am I doing this right?
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much enjoyment out of the things you used to love, like seeing your grandchildren or going to your church group, even if just for a little while?

Oh, heavens, no... I still absolutely adore seeing my grandchildren. They are just the light of my life, truly. And my church group, well, I wouldn't miss it for the world. 

I feel like I keep giving you the exact same answer to this, Doctor, and I'm so sorry if I'm being repetitive or... or if I'm not giving you the answers you're looking for. I just really do still find so much joy in my days. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or hide anything from you, I just genuinely haven't lost my enthusiasm for the people and things I love. 

Is it... is it okay that I don't have that issue? I really do want to be a good patient for you, so I hope it's alright that I keep saying no to this one.
Doctor: Have you found it difficult to start doing things, even things you usually enjoy, not just when you're at the kitchen table?

Oh, no, starting things hasn't been a problem at all. I mean, I still get up and get going every morning, and I'm always happy to get to my little projects or head out to see friends. 

I know we've talked a lot about the kitchen table getting a bit... cluttered, and I know I can get a little sidetracked once I'm doing something, but getting started is really no trouble. I just jump right in! 

I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record, Doctor. I know you have to ask all these questions, and I want to be as helpful as I can. It's just that I really don't struggle with getting myself to do things, especially the things I love. Is that... is that an alright answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.
Have you found it difficult to get started on activities in general, not just when you're at the kitchen table, even when you know you need to do them?

Oh, my. I feel terrible, I think we really are going in circles, aren't we? I am so, so sorry if I'm not explaining myself properly. I'd just hate to think I'm wasting your time. 

But, well, no... getting started really isn't the hard part for me, even for the chores I know I ought to be doing. I can always get up and pull the vacuum out, or gather the laundry... it's just, you know, seeing it all the way through to the end before something else catches my eye. But the actual starting? No, I don't struggle with that at all. 

I do hope you aren't frustrated with me for giving the same sort of answer again. I'm trying my very best to be helpful, I promise. Am I doing okay?
